_comment: Device library. Every marker the editor can place is defined HERE, not in code. Keys are <kind>.<name> without exception — device.camera, fixture.spot, furniture.bed — so the naming rule is one rule and an item that records its kind always resolves on the first lookup. `aliases` maps the older bare names back. Colours are "@token" references resolved against the active theme. A device icon names a DRAWN PATH in lib/shapes.js, never a Unicode character: inside an <svg>, glyphs like the power symbol render as tofu boxes on Windows and Android. Furniture names a shape in the same file, so a bed draws as a bed rather than a rectangle. `render.cone` gives a device a coverage wedge drawn from its own fov/range/rot, and a fixture's `defaults.watt` is what lights its room — see lib/lighting.js.
_aliases_comment: Old bare type keys. Every key in `types` is now `<kind>.<name>`, and an item records its kind, so resolution is kind-first and this table is only reached by an item that never recorded one. Bare names claimed by two kinds (solar, water, washer, tv...) are deliberately absent: guessing which one was meant is exactly the bug the kind field exists to prevent.

device.ac.label: Air conditioner
device.ac._on_rule: climate entities report an hvac_mode, never "on" — anything but "off" counts as running.

props.label: Detection cone
props.hint: Draw what this covers. Off by default — a house with several sensors close together ends up with more wedge than plan. Turning it on is what makes the field of view and range below matter.

props.hint: Safe tokens: {{ value }}, {{ unit }}, {{ name }}, {{ entity }}, and {{ attr.attribute_name }}. Example: {{ value }} °C

props.label: Value thresholds
props.hint: The color for the highest threshold less than or equal to the numeric entity value is used.

device.label._comment: A plain SVG text label bound to any entity. The template is token interpolation only, never executable code. Tap always opens more-info even when the bound domain would normally toggle.

device.temp_sensor.label: Temperature
device.temp_sensor._on_rule: Its state is the reading, not a word — see stateOf() in plan-scene.js.

device.wall_switch.label: Wall switch (1 to 5 gang)
device.wall_switch._comment: One plate, N gangs, each its own entity. Gangs draw from props.channels where bound and fall back to this marker's own entity where not, so a switch is useful before every gang has been wired up. See MARKERS.switch in shapes.js.

device.extension.label: Extension board (multi-outlet)
device.extension._comment: Draws a box with one socket per channel. A single disc cannot say WHICH outlets are live.

device.energy_meter.label: Energy meter
device.energy_meter._on_rule: Its state is the reading, not a word — see stateOf() in plan-scene.js.

furniture.stairs.label: Stairs
furniture.stairs._comment: A flight is architecture: the variant decides how it turns, `steps`/`dir`/`axis` how it is climbed, and `lighting`/`lightEvery` what is lit on it. Bind an entity and the lit parts follow it — `sequence` decides whether they all come up together, as most step lighting does, or climb the flight one step at a time the way a motion-triggered progressive stair light does.

furniture.solar.label: Solar array (furniture)
furniture.solar._comment: One panel by default. cols/rows lay out an array of identical panels inside the footprint — set 2x1 for two side by side, 1x4 for a single file of four. The legacy [cols, rows] `grid` array is still read if present.

logic.automation.label: Automation
logic.automation._comment: On means enabled, not running. An automation you have switched off is the one thing about it worth seeing on a plan.

logic.scene.label: Scene
logic.scene._comment: A scene's state is the last time it was activated, so it is never 'on' and 'unknown' is its normal resting value. onRule momentary keeps a scene nobody has run yet out of the dead style.

logic.script.label: Script / routine
logic.script._comment: A script IS on while it runs, so the default rule is right — and a long-running one lights up, which is exactly what you want to see.

props.label: Service data (JSON)
props.hint: Variables passed when this runs — {"speed": 3}. A script that takes a value needs one marker per value, which is the honest way to draw "set fan to 3".

logic.toggle.label: Toggle helper
logic.toggle._comment: input_boolean. Do-not-disturb, guest mode, holiday. The house's own state, not a device's.

logic.button.label: Button helper
logic.button._comment: input_button / button. Its state is the last press, so like a scene it has no on-state to draw.

logic.number.label: Number helper
logic.number._comment: A threshold, a delay, a setpoint. Its state IS the reading, so numeric — without it a helper sitting at 12 draws in the OFF style with its readout suppressed.

logic.select.label: Dropdown helper
logic.select._comment: A mode: Home / Away / Night. There is no on here, only which option — so the badge carries the answer and the marker never claims a state it does not have.

logic.timer.label: Timer helper
logic.timer._comment: idle / active / paused. `offStates` says which of those is off in one line, rather than a rule name nothing else would ever use.

_roomTypes_comment: A starting point for a room, not a constraint: picking one sets the flooring and whether the room is outdoors, and everything stays editable afterwards. Adding one is a JSON entry — nothing in the renderer knows the word "kitchen".
